long.1: Slow-cooked with butter and a dash of cream, these scrambled eggs stay velvety and rich, forming soft, glossy curds. A sprinkle of salt and pepper is all they need. Spoon them onto a slice of warm rye for a cosy 180 g breakfast that feels both indulgent and effortless.
long.2: Two eggs whipped with a splash of cream cook into a light, custardy omelette studded with sweet tomato dice and soft onion. A quick fold in the pan seals in steam, keeping the centre moist while the outside stays buttery-gold. Served with a slice of toasted rye, it’s a simple 200 g breakfast that balances richness with fresh vegetable brightness.
long.3: Three paper-thin pancakes arrive folded and still warm, ready to be drenched in velvety condensed milk. The custardy crêpes are light yet rich, their edges faintly crisp from butter in the pan. Dip or drizzle-the sweet milk adds creamy caramel notes that turn a simple breakfast into a nostalgic treat.
long.4: Three golden crêpes fold around a pool of bright berry jam, the tart-sweet spread seeping into the soft layers. Butter-kissed edges contrast with fruity freshness, delivering a balanced 230 g breakfast or dessert.
long.5: Two slices of hearty rye bread are lightly toasted, then lavishly spread with smooth berry jam. The contrast of tangy dark crumb and sweet fruit makes for a quick, satisfying 130 g start to the day.
long.6: A comforting 500 g bowl of tender rice grains cooked in milk and water until velvety-soft. Drizzled with golden honey, it offers gentle sweetness and a glossy finish, while crunchy chopped walnuts add nutty depth and textural contrast. Served warm, this classic Russian breakfast feels soothing and nourishing from the first spoonful.
long.7: This warm 500 g bowl of buckwheat porridge blends the nutty flavour of groats with sweet honey and crunchy walnuts. Simmered in milk for a smooth finish, it’s a hearty, comforting way to start the day.
long.8: A comforting 500 g bowl pairs creamy milk-slow-cooked oats with a drizzle of floral honey and a scatter of crunchy walnuts. The result is softly sweet, nutty and richly satisfying-perfect fuel for an energetic morning.
long.9: Slowly simmered in a fragrant broth of onion, garlic, bay leaf and peppercorns, our beef tongue turns meltingly tender. Served in 7–10 slices, tender slices, total of approximately 150–160 g. Each slice tastes delicately beefy, melting gently on the palate. A dab of sharp mustard brightens the flavour, while crisp coins of pickled cucumber cut through the richness with a refreshing crunch. A classic Russian cold appetiser that feels both honest and refined.
long.10: Crunchy cucumbers, tangy white and red cabbage, sweet green apple, juicy tomato and earthy beetroot are lightly brined overnight with garlic, dill and peppercorns. Gentle acidity highlights each vegetable’s natural sweetness, keeping every bite crisp and refreshing. Served chilled as a classic Russian zakuska, it awakens the palate and pairs well with hearty dishes.
long.11: Our Holodec sets shredded beef in a crystal-clear, savoury meat jelly for a cool about 400 gram a portion. The meat is tender yet springy, suspended in silky jelly that carries gentle hints of garlic and bay leaf. Each bite offers mellow beef flavour balanced by the clean, briny snap of a gherkin and the sharp heat of mustard on the side-an authentic Russian appetiser that refreshes the palate and invites the next course.
long.12: Five neat eggplant rolls, about 170 - 190 g total. Showcase smoky fried aubergine wrapped around a cool, creamy garlic-mayonnaise spread. Inside each roll a juicy tomato strip and hint of fresh dill add brightness, while a drizzle of tangy pomegranate molasses and a sprinkle of crushed walnuts bring sweet-sour sparkle and gentle crunch. A vibrant cold appetiser that balances richness with refreshing textures.
long.13: A steaming 500 g bowl of deep-ruby borscht pairs tender beef cubes with sweet beetroot, carrot and potato, all swimming in a lightly tangy broth brightened by tomato paste and a splash of vinegar. Shredded cabbage adds gentle crunch, while fresh dill and a dollop of sour cream round out the classic Slavic flavours. Comforting, colourful and satisfyingly earthy.
long.14: A comforting 500 g bowl features tender egg noodles, sweet carrot and bell pepper, and shreds of succulent chicken swimming in clear golden broth. Fresh dill lends a bright herbal lift, while a touch of black pepper warms every spoonful. It’s the classic cure-all soup: light yet satisfying, perfect for any day that needs a little home-cooked warmth.
long.15: A hearty 500 g bowl of meatball soup delivers tender beef meatballs alongside diced potato, carrot, onion, and bell pepper in a savoury broth. Fresh dill adds an aromatic finish, lifting each spoonful with herbal brightness. Simple, wholesome, and deeply comforting, it’s the kind of soup that warms from within and feels just like home.
long.16: A chilled 500 g bowl of Okroshka combines tender cubes of cooked beef, boiled potatoes, crisp cucumber, and chopped eggs in a tangy yogurt broth, gently fizzed with soda water. Fresh dill and creamy sour cream round out the flavours, creating a vibrant, refreshing soup perfect for warm days. Every spoonful offers creamy coolness and a satisfying crunch.
long.17: A hearty 340 g bowl of solyanka layers tender beef cubes and smoky sausages in a bright tomato broth sharpened with pickled cucumbers, olives and a squeeze of lemon. Each spoonful delivers a lively balance of savoury meat, briny vegetables and fresh dill aroma-comforting yet refreshingly tangy.
long.18: About 300 g of colourful diced potatoes, carrots and sweet green peas mingle with tangy gherkins, tender cubes of beef and chopped egg. A smooth, lightly seasoned mayonnaise ties everything together, adding gentle richness without masking the fresh crunch. Each spoonful balances savoury meat, vegetable sweetness and a bright hint of pickle brine-Russia’s beloved holiday salad, cooling yet hearty.
long.19: A 300 g bowl of classic vinegret layers jewel-red beetroot, tender potato and carrot with tangy gherkins and sauerkraut. Fresh dill and a splash of vinegar lift the earthy sweetness, while sunflower oil gives a silky finish. Every forkful delivers crisp, briny pops against mellow root-veg cubes-refreshing yet satisfying, and a beloved staple of Russian home cooking.
long.20: A neat 300 g round reveals classic Shuba layers: soft potato base, sweet carrot, salty diced herring and vivid beetroot, all lightly bound with mayonnaise and finished with fluffy grated egg. The cool slice offers earthy sweetness, gentle brine and creamy richness in every forkful-a festive burst of colour and unmistakably Russian flavour.
long.21: A crisp 300 g serving of shakarob marries equal parts juicy tomato, crunchy cucumber and fragrant onion ribbons. Fresh dill threads through the mix, while a simple splash of olive oil and vinegar adds silky body and gentle tang. Light, vibrant and irresistibly refreshing, this Central-Asian staple wakes up the palate and pairs beautifully with grilled meats or hearty mains.
long.22: A lively 300 g mix of paper-thin tomato and cucumber slices is laced with sharp onion and fresh chili rings. A quick salt toss draws out natural juices, creating a light, tangy dressing that lets garden freshness shine while adding a gentle bite of heat. Crisp, juicy and wonderfully simple, Achichuk is the perfect cool counterpart to rich plov or grilled meats.
long.23: A bright 300 g heap of freshly grated carrots glistens in a light sunflower-oil dressing sharpened with white vinegar and scented with warm ground coriander. Tiny flecks of sweet onion tuck between the strands, adding a gentle bite. The result is crunchy, lightly tangy and herb-fragrant-a simple Russian salad that cleanses the palate and pairs effortlessly with rich main courses.
long.24: A generous 400 g bowl overflows with juicy tomatoes, crisp cucumber and sweet bell pepper, offset by ribbons of pungent red onion. Briny Kalamata-style olives and creamy feta cubes lend salty depth, while a bright dressing of extra-virgin olive oil, lemon juice and oregano lightly coats every bite. Fresh, colourful and perfectly balanced, this timeless Mediterranean salad brings sunny flavours to any table.
long.25: Warm, pepper-seared beef slices crown a colourful mix of cucumber, bell pepper, tomato and onion. A tangy soy-chili-lime dressing adds heat and brightness, turning the 330 g bowl into a lively balance of juicy meat and crunchy vegetables-light enough for lunch, bold enough to satisfy a steak craving.
long.26: A crisp, glossy crust gives way to a moist, mildly sweet filling of sautéed white cabbage, carrot and a whisper of fresh dill. The tender yeast-raised dough bakes up airy yet resilient, keeping every bite light while adding a gentle buttery note. Served warm, this 160 g Russian pie delivers comforting home-kitchen flavours-earthy vegetables wrapped in flaky bread, perfect for breakfast or a quick snack on the go.
long.27: A 300 g mound of sweet, ruby beetroot is gently bound with creamy mayonnaise and dotted with soft diced prunes for a subtle fruit note. Tangy feta slices crown the top, while chopped walnuts add a toasty crunch. Earthy sweetness, mellow creaminess and nutty depth mingle in every forkful, making this colourful Russian classic an instant table brightener.
long.28: A 160 g golden pie hides a cosy filling of buttery potato, sautéed mushrooms and fresh dill. The lightly sweet yeast dough bakes up airy yet sturdy, offering a soft crumb beneath its crisp, egg-washed crust. Earthy vegetables and fragrant herbs meet gentle sweetness in each bite, making this baked Russian classic perfect for breakfast on the go or a comforting snack with tea.
long.29: A golden, 160 g samsa features crisp, flaky pastry wrapped around juicy ground beef, sweet onion and warm cumin. Each bite delivers buttery layers that shatter to reveal savoury filling, lightly perfumed with spice and black pepper heat. Enjoy fresh from the oven with a side of fiery ajika for a true Central-Asian street-stall experience.
long.30: A crescent of fluffy milk dough hides a ribbon of sweet-tart berry jam. Sesame-dusted crust gives gentle crunch, while the inside remains light and slightly chewy-perfect with morning coffee or as an afternoon treat.
long.31: A juicy chicken frank is spiralled in sweet, buttery milk dough and baked until the crust turns shiny amber. Inside, the bread stays pillow-soft, sealing in sausage juices so every bite offers savoury snap and airy crumb-street-food comfort straight from the oven.
long.32: A round milk-dough bun cradles a creamy filling of lightly sweetened cottage cheese. Baked until the rim turns glossy amber and the centre sets souffle-soft, this 170 g pastry offers contrasting textures: pillowy crumb, silky cheese and a kiss of powdered sugar.
long.33: Three tender Russian crêpes, rolled around savoury shredded beef, make up a satisfying ≈ 290 g serving. The paper-thin pancakes stay soft yet slightly crisp at the edges, while the warm meat filling lends hearty richness. A cool spoonful of sour cream on the side adds creamy tang, turning this simple street-style snack into true comfort food.
long.34: Three delicate crêpes, rolled around savoury sautéed mushrooms, make a comforting ≈ 290 g serving. The pancakes stay tender with lightly crisp edges, while the earthy mushroom filling adds umami depth. A cool spoonful of sour cream lends creamy tang, turning this homestyle Russian favourite into a simple yet satisfying bite.
long.35: A generous ≈ 380 g helping of vareniki delivers pillowy dough pockets stuffed with creamy potato, sweet onion and a hint of dill. Each dumpling is boiled until tender, then glossed with melted butter so the wrappers stay silky. Add a spoon of cool sour cream for contrast and you get the ultimate Slavic comfort-simple, soothing and impossible to stop at one.
long.36: A hearty 360 g bowl holds about twenty petite pelmeni: thin, springy dough envelopes juicy minced beef scented with onion, garlic and a whisper of cumin. Each dumpling bursts with savoury broth as you bite, while a slick of sunflower oil keeps the wrappers silky. Pair them with a cool spoon of sour cream for classic Russian comfort that’s equal parts delicate and satisfying.
long.37: Three golden-edged draniki-together about 280 g-deliver the comforting crunch of grated potatoes bound with a hint of onion. The interior stays soft and fluffy, while the outside turns addictively crisp from a quick pan-fry. A cool spoonful of rich sour cream melts over the hot surface, adding creamy tang that lifts the mild earthy flavour. Simple, satisfying and perfect straight from the skillet.
long.38: A hearty 450 g plate brings four-to-five plump manti: silky, springy dough parcels stuffed with juicy minced beef, sweet onion and warm cumin. Steaming locks the flavours inside, so each bite releases aromatic juices that mingle with a gloss of melted butter. A cool spoon of sour cream on the side adds creamy tang, turning this Central-Asian classic into pure comfort.
long.39: A single 170 g cheburek arrives piping-hot: a thin, blistered pastry pocket that crackles as you bite. Inside, juicy minced beef mingles with sweet onion and warm cumin, releasing aromatic steam. The dough is light yet sturdy, holding savoury juices without turning greasy. Served with zingy adjika on the side, this Uzbek-inspired street classic is all about crispy crust and flavour-packed meat.
long.40: Two pan-seared 100 g beef cutlets stay tender thanks to a splash of cream and grated onion worked into the mince. Ground cumin and coriander lend gentle warmth, while a quick fry in oil gives a crisp, golden crust that seals in the juices. Pair them with either buttery mashed potato or nutty buckwheat and a spoon of mushroom sauce for a classic Russian main that balances comfort and spice.
long.41: Two 100 g chicken cutlets stay tender thanks to cream and onion blended into the mince, while a pinch of cumin and coriander adds subtle warmth. Quickly pan-seared for a crisp bronze crust, they’re finished through so the centre stays moist. Pair them with creamy mashed potato or nutty buckwheat and a spoon of mushroom sauce for a comforting, homestyle main.
long.42: Tender beef cubes, sweet julienned carrots and nutty chickpeas simmer beneath a blanket of cumin-scented rice, absorbing rich beef broth and the perfume of a whole garlic head. Each forkful delivers fluffy grains, juicy meat and gentle spice-comforting yet deeply aromatic. Enjoy the 400 g mound piping-hot with a side of refreshing achichuk salad for true Uzbek hospitality.
long.43: Tender cabbage leaves wrap a savory blend of minced beef, rice and sweet onion, then slow-bake for two hours in a light tomato broth until everything melds into silky comfort. Each 400 g serving delivers juicy meat, fluffy grains and melt-soft cabbage bathed in tangy sauce - a Russian-style classic perfect for chilly days.
long.44: Arriving on a steaming cast-iron pan, this 400 g “hot-pan” mingles seared beef strips with golden potato cubes, earthy mushrooms and sweet onion. A quick toss with fresh spring onion and dill lifts the hearty flavours, while a light gloss of vegetable oil keeps each bite juicy and fragrant. Simple, rustic and deeply satisfying, it’s comfort food that crackles all the way to the table.
long.45: Thin ribbons of tenderloin are flash-seared, then finished in a silky mushroom-cream sauce scented with sweet onions. Rich yet quick-cooked, the dish melts in the mouth and begs to be paired with a soft bed of mashed potato or nutty buckwheat-two traditional sides that soak up every drop of sauce.
long.46: Crisp breadcrumb crust hides a pocket of herb-dill butter that melts into juicy chicken with the first cut. Lightly spiced and pan-fried, then finished in the oven, this 220 g Kiev balances crunchy exterior with rich, aromatic centre. Pair it with creamy mash or nutty buckwheat to soak up every drop of sizzling butter.
long.47: Dozens of feather-light puff-pastry layers cradle a buttery caramel cream enriched with toasted walnuts. Each 200 g slice marries crisp, shattering sheets with a nut-speckled filling that melts into mellow sweetness, giving the classic Napoleon a subtle crunch and deep, creamy finish. Best after a slow chill, when the pastry softens just enough to cut cleanly while still delivering its signature flake.
long.48: A moist 160 g slice of honey cake greets you with buttery aroma and a warm amber crumb. Gentle notes of floral honey run through the tender sponge, while tiny dice of prune add soft pockets of fruity sweetness. A whisper-thin caramel glaze seals the top, giving each bite a glossy finish that melts on the tongue. Enjoy on its own or with a spoon of thick sour cream for a truly nostalgic Russian dessert.
long.49: Three delicate Russian crêpes, rolled around mildly sweet cottage cheese, create a cosy ≈ 280 g treat. The pancakes stay tender with lacy edges, while the creamy filling adds gentle tang and protein-rich body. Finish with a splash of berry jam or condensed milk for a touch of sweetness, and you have a comforting dessert that feels both light and nostalgic.
long.50: Five petite syrniki - a cosy ≈ 150 g portion - pair a fluffy cottage-cheese centre with a delicate, caramel-kissed crust. Lightly sweet and scented with vanilla, each cake offers creamy tang inside and gentle crunch outside. Finish with a spoon of sour cream, berry jam or silky condensed milk for a timeless Slavic dessert that feels both wholesome and indulgent.
long.51: A single 220 g skewer of chicken breast is marinated in lemon juice, Dijon and fragrant coriander, then char-grilled until the edges caramelise while the inside stays juicy. The creamy mayo glaze locks in moisture and carries the citrus-pepper tang into every bite. Finish with tomato-garlic sauce or crisp veggies for a bright, protein-packed grill favourite.
long.52: A single 220 g skewer showcases pepper-rubbed beef tenderloin seared over open flame. The quick marinade of oil, salt and black pepper lets the natural richness of the meat shine, while high-heat grilling creates a smoky crust and rosy, tender centre. Rested briefly to keep the juices in, it’s ready for dipping in tomato-garlic sauce or pairing with crisp vegetables.
long.53: A 220 g skewer of lamb tenderloin is marinated in creamy mayo, Dijon and a bold mix of cumin and coriander, then seared over open flame until the edges char and the centre stays juicy. The warm spices infuse each bite with earthy aroma, while the light glaze keeps the meat succulent. Pair with tomato-garlic sauce or crisp vegetables for a richly flavoured grill favourite.
long.54: A full-kilogram platter brings the best of the grill: peppery beef tenderloin skewer, zesty lemon-coriander chicken, spice-rubbed lamb, a juicy lyulya kebab and a perfectly charred lamb chop. Each cut is cooked over open flame, rested for peak juiciness, then served together for easy sharing. Paired with tomato-garlic sauce, fries and crisp cucumber–onion salad, this feast offers smoky aromas, varied textures and bold, harmonious flavours in every bite.
long.55: Nutty buckwheat is gently simmered until each grain turns tender but remains distinct, then finished with a pat of butter for silky richness. The 300 g bowl delivers earthy flavour, light texture and satisfying warmth-an ideal Russian side that pairs effortlessly with stews, cutlets or grilled meats.
long.56: A 200 g lyulya kebab blends beef topside and chicken breast with sweet onion, cumin and coriander, then grills over open flame until the outside chars and the inside stays juicy. The mix of meats gives balanced richness and tenderness, while warm spices leave a subtle, earthy aroma. Serve straight off the skewer with tomato-garlic sauce and crisp veggies for a true Caucasian-style grill experience.
long.57: Two thick lamb chops-about 380 g total-are brushed with oil, salt and cracked pepper, then seared over open flame until the fat crisps and the meat turns blush-pink inside. The minimal seasoning lets the natural, slightly sweet flavour of young lamb shine, while a brief rest keeps each bite juicy. Pair with tomato-garlic sauce and crisp veggies for a rustic mixed-grill classic.
long.58: Tender long-grain rice is gently steamed, then finished with a pat of butter for a silky sheen and subtle richness. The 300 g side delivers perfectly separate grains with a light, buttery aroma-an adaptable pairing for stews, grills or sautéed vegetables.
long.59: A colourful medley of peppers, onion, tomato and mushrooms hits the grill, picking up charred edges and sweet smoky notes. Finished with a gloss of melted butter, the vegetables stay juicy inside while the skins blister for extra flavour. This 350 g side dish brings brightness, texture and a hint of fire-kissed richness to any main course.
long.60: Slim wedges of sweet potato are tossed in light oil and smoked paprika, then roasted until caramel-edged and tender inside. The result is a 200 g basket of naturally sweet, gently spiced fries with a crisp bite-perfect alongside burgers, grilled meats or enjoyed solo with your favourite dip.
long.61: Fluffy, velvety potatoes are whipped with sweet cream and a generous knob of butter to create a silky purée that melts on the tongue. A pinch of salt and cracked pepper lift the natural earthy sweetness, making this 300 g side the perfect partner for rich mains or a comforting bite all on its own.
long.62: Twice-fried for perfect crunch, these 200 g fries boast a shatter-crisp exterior and fluffy centre. A quick soak removes starch, while the two-stage fry-first low, then hot-locks in golden colour and irresistible texture. Sprinkle with salt and enjoy on their own or alongside your favourite main.
long.63: Pan-fried potato cubes mingle with juicy mushrooms, sweet onion and bright spring onion, all tossed in aromatic oil and finished with fresh dill. The result is a generous, about-500 g side: crisp-edged potatoes outside, fluffy within, balanced by earthy mushroom depth and a herbal lift-pure homestyle comfort alongside any grilled meat or enjoyed on its own.
long.64: Fresh from the oven, this 160 g round flatbread boasts a chewy, airy crumb and a lightly blistered crust dotted with nutty sesame seeds. Brushed with sunflower oil for softness, it offers a gentle sweetness from milk and sugar balanced by a savoury edge of sea salt. Tear it apart to reveal steam and enjoy alongside soups, grilled meats or simply on its own.
long.65: A punchy blend of bell pepper, hot chili and garlic, brightened with herbs and vinegar. Spoon over grilled meats or flatbread for an instant hit of heat and freshness.
long.66: Tangy ketchup meets silky mayo, crunchy pickle and a hint of paprika: a versatile, mildly sweet sauce that flatters burgers, grilled meats or fried potatoes.
long.67: Smooth Dijon and creamy mayo meet honey’s sweetness and vinegary bite, creating a balanced mustard sauce that pairs with chicken cutlets, fries or grilled veg.
long.68: Slow-simmered ketchup and paste gain depth from fresh garlic, vinegar and herbs. Ideal with skewers, fries or baked pies.
long.76: A chilled 250 ml glass of raspberry mors bursts with the vivid colour and sweet-tart flavour of summer berries. Lightly sweetened and gently extracted, it offers a refreshing sip that quenches thirst while delivering a subtle hint of natural fruit pulp.
long.77: A chilled 250 ml glass of ruby-red mors delivers the pure, tart essence of cranberries balanced by a touch of sugar. Light, fruity and thirst-quenching, it’s the classic Russian way to cool down and boost your vitamin C.
